cli.root.short: Automatic backup of Claude data and projects to two encrypted copies
cli.root.long:
BackUpClaude saves Claude's data every hour and your projects every day to two encrypted copies: one on a local disk and one in external storage.

This is an unofficial project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

cli.backup.long:
Saves a profile to the local repository: claude is Claude's data, projects is the working folders found in transcripts and your own folders. Without --profile both run. With --dry-run the files are read and nothing is stored.
Files another program holds are listed. Exit code 1 means something is missing from the snapshot.

cli.verify.long: Reads the file tree of the latest snapshot of a profile and compares it with the disk. Exit code 1 means something is missing or something banned got in.

cli.schedule.short: Put the automatic runs into the Windows Task Scheduler
cli.schedule.long: Creates, shows and removes the scheduled tasks: Claude's data every hour, projects every day, cleanup, check and the summary every week by default. The intervals come from the settings. The tasks run as you, without administrator rights, show no window and catch up after the computer was off.

cli.restore.long:
Brings back one session (--session), one project (--project) or everything (--all) from a copy. By default the files go to a new folder next to the local repository and nothing in place changes. With --apply the missing files are also put back where they were; a file that exists is never replaced. Without flags the command asks questions and shows the latest sessions.

On a new computer: backupclaude restore --repo <where the copy is> --all, then type the password from paper.
flag.restore.session: id of the session or its first characters (see list --sessions)
flag.restore.project: project: its folder name, a part of it or the full path
flag.restore.all: everything of the newest snapshots: Claude's data and the projects
flag.restore.from: copy to restore from: local or offsite
flag.restore.snapshot: snapshot id (see list --snapshots); the newest by default
flag.restore.to: folder to restore into; by default a new folder next to the local repository
flag.restore.apply: also put the missing files back in place; existing files are never replaced
flag.restore.dry_run: with --apply: show what would be put back and change nothing in place
flag.restore.map: OLD=NEW: move a folder of the old computer, for example D:\Work=E:\Work (may repeat)
flag.restore.repo: repository to restore from without settings: a folder or an rclone:/sftp: address
flag.restore.password_stdin: read the repository password from the first line of the input
restore.one_mode.hint: Restore one thing at a time, or run restore without flags to answer questions.
restore.dry_run_needs_apply.hint: A restore without --apply changes nothing in place anyway: it only writes a new folder.

restore.session_bad_id.hint: A session id looks like 0fc6092b-f4d7-460e-ab01-acc244289ebe; at least the first 6 characters are needed. See backupclaude list --sessions.
